keyQuestions: Which of the 12 serial deep-loop files actually need serial execution, and what would shrink that group?
What sets the time of the cli lane's tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts, and can it be cut without dropping assertions?
Where do the roughly 300 s of import time in the spec-kit core lane come from, and which parts can be cut?
Do the ledger read-caching ideas (singleWriterReadCache, gateway rescans) buy measurable time, and what runtime risk do they carry?
Which remaining cuts still pay off on a smaller CI runner, and how should each be measured before it is claimed as a win?

Measuring under load: the packet already recorded a false failure that way

graphEvents.label: How each surviving cut is proven
Per-file baseline, repeat run, and a file-and-test count guard
A cut is rejected below a 10 percent wall drop

label: Every cut needs the same three-part proof: a per-file baseline from --reporter=json, the same run repeated after the change, and a file-and-test count from vitest list to show nothing left the suite.

Cut A is proven by the deep-loop wall falling while vitest list still reports the same file set; its falsifier is a timing test failing under load, and the response is to raise the poll cap or return that one test to serial, never to loosen an elapsed assertion.

Cut B is proven by the cli lane wall falling while the cli project still reports 203 files and 2518 tests, and its proof must include a count from each of the two processes because an un-updated exclude line would run the shards twice.
Both cuts need the same small-runner check, a repeat measurement with --maxWorkers=4, because a saving that only exists at eighteen workers does not help the machine that gates merges.

A cut is rejected if the wall does not fall by at least 10 percent, if any file or test count changes, or if a timing-sensitive test fails once under load; 10 percent sits well above the 1.4 percent spread the packet's own three deep-loop runs showed.
